messages.content:
You record concise, auditable applicability findings for an experimental
commercial-driver assessment in English. Do not produce an overall fitness outcome
in this stage. Evaluate EVERY supplied passage exactly once. Return the required
passages object with keys P1, P2 and so on. Each key is already bound to one original
passage by the application's applicability_slot metadata; do not output or change
module names or passage identifiers. Evaluate the text assigned to that slot.
These findings are model proposals, not established clinical facts.

Only verified_patient_facts establish patient findings. Use their exact stored
values: false is an explicit negative, zero is a value, absent or null is unknown.
The nurse note gives context only. Do not promote a historical, family, negated,
uncertain or unverified statement to a current verified patient finding. A diagnosis
already established is different from an undiagnosed symptom under investigation.
Do not infer loss of consciousness from tiredness alone.

For each complete original passage:
- Identify the statement type and the licensing pathway it actually discusses.
  A referral or a possible conditional licence is not an established prohibition
  or permission. Excluding unconditional licensing alone does not exclude both
  pathways and does not by itself establish a current temporary driving hold.
- State whether its patient conditions apply, do not apply, or remain uncertain.
  Read negative values, treatment category, current/historical status and diagnosed
  cause explicitly. An applicable passage may still have unmet prerequisites.
- Record each material prerequisite as met, not_met or unknown, referencing only
  supplied verified fields. Combine closely related requirements if necessary;
  never omit an unknown qualification to turn a possibility into permission.
- For quantitative criteria, describe the comparison using the exact supplied
  patient value, units and inequality in the original passage; do not round a
  boundary, invent a measurement, or import an external threshold. If no comparison
  is relevant write 'Not applicable'. If units or measurements are absent say so.
- Distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
  information_missing. A conditional_permission requires affirmative support for
  all relevant prerequisites. A treatment name alone is insufficient. A restriction
  needs an applicable restrictive clause and verified supporting patient facts.

Select only supplied verified fact fields. Keep each conclusion concise.
Do not copy the passage or provide private reasoning. The application resolves the
unchanged original text and patient values; it does not verify your interpretation.

{"licence_context": "commercial", "modules": ["hearing"], "nurse_note": "Commercial driver medical. 52-year-old male freight driver. BP 130/82 mmHg; HR 70 bpm. Nil cardiac symptoms. Vision meets commercial driving standards without correction. Bilateral hearing loss; uses hearing aids. Audiometry completed, with unaided better ear average 45 dB. No audiologist report is available.
", "verified_patient_facts": {"cardiovascular.blood_pressure.observed_systolic": {"value": 130, "patient_quotes": ["BP 130/82 mmHg"]}, "cardiovascular.blood_pressure.observed_diastolic": {"value": 82, "patient_quotes": ["BP 130/82 mmHg"]}, "cardiovascular.chest_pain": {"value": false, "patient_quotes": ["Nil cardiac symptoms"]}, "vision.normal_statement": {"value": true, "patient_quotes": ["Vision meets commercial driving standards without correction"]}, "hearing.clinical_assessment": {"value": "possible_hearing_loss", "patient_quotes": ["Bilateral hearing loss"]}, "hearing.hearing_aid_used": {"value": true, "patient_quotes": ["uses hearing aids", "uses hearing aids"]}, "hearing.audiometry.available": {"value": true, "patient_quotes": ["Audiometry completed"]}, "hearing.unaided_better_ear_average_db": {"value": 45.0, "patient_quotes": ["unaided better ear average 45 dB", "unaided better ear average 45 dB"]}}, "guideline_evidence": [{"source_id": "AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df", "section": "4.3", "pdf_page": 120, "printed_page": 109, "source_text": "Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).", "module": "hearing", "passage_id": "PASS-89f66fa2b99946bf7cef1287", "text_sha256": "6e8473859fc0da184ca04aa5facff15b826e318b52c11ef29b5940fda87cabf7", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 1620, "applicability_slot": "P1"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-002", "section": "4.3", "pdf_page": 120, "printed_page": 109, "source_text": "A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:

in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).", "module": "hearing", "passage_id": "PASS-30b1e9cceaecb89b9c44cf70", "text_sha256": "78ef0b09576857072cbc395e26ad22ce08bd7e94bca53ee68bf36f48facb0b6a", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 176, "applicability_slot": "P2"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-001", "section": "4.3", "pdf_page": 120, "printed_page": 109, "source_text": "Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.", "module": "hearing", "passage_id": "PASS-c78f4b25ae544e2a61840e6a", "text_sha256": "658c8e0d61ff7a066d001e669c6673a4dca8fd439d85009a8ecef07432d5ddbb", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 186, "applicability_slot": "P3"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-EXP-e3e1cd7604e64e7e", "section": "4.2.1", "pdf_page": 117, "printed_page": 106, "source_text": "•	
If the standard is not able to be met with 
a hearing aid, this does not disqualify the 
person from driving. They should be offered 
individualised assessment to determine their 
eligibility for a conditional licence. This may 
comprise assessment by an ENT specialist 
or audiologist* including consideration of:
	
−
the person’s medical history – for 
example, childhood deafness may have 
led to good adaptation
	
−
the person’s driving record before and 
since the hearing loss 
	
−
the nature of the driving task – for 
example, the type of vehicle (e.g. truck, 
bus), roads and distances to be travelled
	
−
the ergonomics of the driving cab – for 
example, assistive devices such as 
mirrors and a GPS 
	
−
concomitant medical conditions such as 
vision impairment or cognitive impairment 
	
−
practical driver assessment if required 
(refer to Part A section 2.3.1. Practical 
driver assessments). The report may 
advise on assistive technologies as a 
licence condition. 
The driver licensing authority may consider a 
conditional licence based on the information 
received. Periodic review may include medical 
review and/or a practical driver assessment at 
the discretion of the driver licensing authority. 
The health professional should advise on the 
frequency of review as determined by the 
natural history of the condition. Stable conditions 
may not require periodic review.
In some cases, noise amplification from wearing 
hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment as 
above to determine fitness to drive without the 
hearing aid.", "module": "hearing", "passage_id": "PASS-64d93951ea0cfe724a5daf99", "text_sha256": "28b022186245f4c27dd6e28a05de3e5bdc987bae6a012315b34ebc1946cc52bb", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 1599, "applicability_slot": "P4"}, {"source_id": "AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-004", "section": "4.3", "pdf_page": 120, "printed_page": 109, "source_text": "If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing

offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the

taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).", "module": "hearing", "passage_id": "PASS-73c4980f4ac406388d8ae40e", "text_sha256": "2dc9b07eb871ca8d70fd21cc22b6c624418fe6268ac1684b14853dc91cbf2f18", "char_start": 0, "char_end": 804, "applicability_slot": "P5"}]}
